notes:
Refer to EWZ documents for details. According to photocopy #1542, Wilhelm was 163 cm or, 5'4" tall, weighed 64.5 kg or 142.19 pounds, wore glasses, was of slender build, had blue eyes and blond hair. The German document was dated 1940 and Wilhelm was born in 1887, so the above would have been his statistics at about age 53 years of age.

EWZ document #1758 says:
"Zelmer, Wilhelm, Farmer, born 12/01/1887 in Klein Gluscha, Kr. Kowel.

Citizenship: Polish. Racial background: Arian.

Married in 1913 Rozyszcze. Applying for citizenship? Yes.

Parents: Friedrich Wilhelm, born ? in Kalish. Evangelical, died in Klein Gluscha.
Ernestine, nee Schulz, born ? in  Kalish.

Wife: Julie, nee Tepper, born 23/11/1891 in Gr. Glusha, Ev.
Parents: Gottlieb, born? in Petrikau, Ev, died in Gr. Gluscha
Julie, nee Schindel, born ar..?Near Lodz, ev, died in Gr. Glusha

Children:
- Friedrich 6/12/1924 in Podborodsche V.21949
- Lucia      7/13/1927 "           "             V.21950
- Ewald    20/11/1932 "          "             V.21956
- Edmund  4/04/1935 "           "             V.21952

Moved on 5/01/1940 from Podborodsche to Pabianice.
Statement dated 8/1/1940 at Lodz."


Refer also to EWZ document #1760, which provides a statement made by Wilhelm Zelmer:
"Appearing is the Volksdeutsche Wilhelm Zelmer from Volhynia, identified by his Polish passport and the following identification card showing him as an adherent of German customs and traditions: No. 21947, wife 21948, Children 21949,50,51,52, and he declared:

"I refer to the statements I made on the attached form and believe these to be correct. My citizenship is as follows: formerly Polish. I apply for myself and those of my family members listed on the attached form to be accedted into German statehood. Our primary language is German. I and my family including children are members of the Evangelical church. My marriage was performed by the same church. I am a member of the following Volksdeutsche associations: (none listed).""


Refer also to EWZ document #1762-1 wherein Wilhelm states:
"I attest in a statutory declaration that all information about myself and my family are true and especially affirm, that I have no knowledge of any facts which would cast a doubt on the German bloodlines of myself and my family and which would point out any influence of Jewish blood.

I and my family members who are also to become citizens, have none, or suffered conviction for the following crimes: (none), are still involved in the following pending judicial processes (political or nonpolitical): (none).

I last resided in Podborodsche, Kreis Kamien-Kosierski and have lived outside the former state of Poland from 1917-1921 in Germany, Hannover, later in Posen, Kreis (undecipherable).

I have been emphatically advised that my citizenship could be declared null and void, and my citizenship certificate could be confiscated, if I had made false declarations about myself and lthe members of my family-or about possible convictions or outstanding court cases.

I am presenting the following records: Document signed by Wilhelm Zelmer and Admission Officer."


See also EWZ document 1762-2, 1764, 1766 and 1768 which are not transcribed here.


See also EWZ document 1542, not all of which is transcribed here, but which says that Wilhelm was examined on Jan 8, 1940, that he had 9 children, 6 of which are living, Evangelical, farmer. His history says that he had bleeding of the lungs 12 years ago, and still has breathing difficulties.  In 1918 the left leg was amputated due to TB of the bone.  His innoculations included smallpox, typhoid and cholera. He was 163cm tall and weighed 64.5kg. His physical condition was deemed to be poor and he was noted to be capable of light work only.  He is described as having blue eyes, blond, plain hairstyle, straight nose and medium long headshape.


See EWZ document 1544 for photograph of Wilhelm Zelmer, scanned and reproduced above.
